summary: The article provides generally accurate and well-supported financial advice for Gen Z in India, emphasizing early investing, SIPs, and debt management.

claims.claim: The interest paid on education loans can be claimed as a deduction under Section 80E of the Income Tax Act, 1961, for a maximum of 8 years.
claims.note: Section 80E allows deduction on interest paid on education loans for a maximum of 8 years. There is no upper limit on the amount of interest that can be claimed.

claims.claim: A SIP allows you to invest a fixed amount regularly (e.g., monthly) into a mutual fund scheme. You can start SIPs with amounts as low as ₹500, making it accessible even with a limited income.
claims.note: AMFI states that SIP installment amounts can be as little as ₹500 per month. Some mutual funds even offer SIPs starting from ₹100.

claims.claim: For most Gen Z investors, direct equity investing might be too time-consuming and require significant research. Equity mutual funds, managed by professional fund managers, offer a convenient way to gain exposure to the stock market. Within equity funds, consider: Diversified Equity Funds and Index Funds. For long-term wealth creation, index funds can be a very effective and low-cost option. You can find more information on mutual funds and their performance on the AMFI India website.
claims.note: AMFI India website provides information on mutual funds and their performance.

claims.claim: A common budgeting rule is the 50/30/20 rule: 50% for Needs, 30% for Wants, 20% for Savings and Debt Repayment.
claims.note: The 50/30/20 rule is a widely recognized budgeting method.

claims.claim: Index Funds: These are passive funds that aim to replicate the performance of a specific market index (e.g., Nifty 50, Sensex 30) by investing in the same stocks in the same proportion. They typically have lower expense ratios than actively managed funds. For long-term wealth creation, index funds can be a very effective and low-cost option.
claims.note: Index funds tracking Nifty 50 or Sensex typically have lower expense ratios (e.g., 0.15%-0.40%) compared to actively managed funds.

article_title: Gen Z: Harnessing Your 20s for Early Wealth Creation
